Thread Characteristics
Thread is a lightweight process.
Represents a single sequence of execution.
Threads share memory and resources of the parent process.
Used to achieve parallelism inside applications.
Example: Browser tabs, text editor spell-checking and formatting.

Multitasking vs Multithreading
Feature | Multitasking | Multithreading
Definition | Execution of more than one process simultaneously. | Process divided into smaller threads running concurrently.
Concept | Multiple processes context switched by OS. | Multiple threads inside the same process.

Memory | Each process has separate memory and resources. | Threads share memory and resources of same process.

multiple sub-queues based on process
properties like priority or type. Each
queue has its own scheduling algorithm.
Fixed Assignment

Example: System processes (SP) use RR, Interactive
processes (IP) use RR, Batch processes (BP) use FCFS.
Fixed Priority Preemptive
Scheduling among queues is fixed-priority preemptive
(e.g., foreground has absolute priority over background).
Starvation & Convoy Effect
Lower priority processes can starve, and the convoy effect
is present.
